s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive systemic disease with autoimmune features, characterized by skin thickening, joint involvement, and internal organ dysfunction
key_facts: Progressive increase in abdominal girth over the last month
Weight loss of 10 kg over the past 12 months
Skin thickening over the last 5 years
Dry, thickened skin with salt-and-pepper lesions on the face
Hardened and hyperpigmented skin on the limbs
Arthritis in the hands with ulnar deviation of the wrists
Interstitial lung disease on Computed Tomography
Intermediate probability of pulmonary hypertension on Echocardiography
Decreased tear secretion on Schirmer test
Increased collagen and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate on skin biopsies

shortlist.label: Systemic Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Skin thickening, joint involvement, and internal organ dysfunction are characteristic of this disease

shortlist.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Positive antinuclear antibodies, low Complement C3, and systemic symptoms are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Overlap of systemic sclerosis, lupus, and rheumatoid arthritis features, with positive antinuclear antibodies and low Complement C3

shortlist.label: Sjögren's Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Ocular dryness, decreased tear secretion, and systemic symptoms are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Limited Systemic Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Skin thickening, Raynaud phenomenon, and esophageal dysmotility are characteristic of this disease, with a more limited scope than systemic sclerosis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including skin thickening, Raynaud phenomenon, and interstitial lung disease, along with laboratory findings such as positive antinuclear antibodies and low Complement C3, are most consistent with Systemic Sclerosis. The presence of hardened and hyperpigmented skin on the limbs, arthritis in the hands, and bilateral pleural effusion further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: While the patient has some features of SLE, such as positive antinuclear antibodies and low Complement C3, the overall clinical picture is more consistent with Systemic Sclerosis.

rejected.label: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not meet the criteria for Mixed Connective Tissue Disease, which typically requires a combination of features from multiple autoimmune diseases.

rejected.label: Sjögren's Syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has ocular dryness, which is a feature of Sjögren's Syndrome, the overall clinical picture is more consistent with Systemic Sclerosis.

rejected.label: Limited Systemic Sclerosis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms, including interstitial lung disease and significant internal organ involvement, are not consistent with Limited Systemic Sclerosis, which is typically characterized by a more limited disease course.

gold: Overlap syndrome involving diffuse systemic sclerosis and systemic lupus erythematosus
